Partial gamma DIF

Source: R/dif_partgam.R
RMdifGamma.Rd

Computes the partial gamma coefficient of each item, the association between the item and a grouping variable given the total score, to assess differential item functioning (DIF). With the result of RMdifGammaCutoff(), it tests each item against simulations without DIF, by default with a bootstrap p-value corrected across items.

Usage

RMdifGamma(
  data,
  dif_var,
  cutoff = NULL,
  p_value = NULL,
  correction = c("fwer", "fdr_bh", "fdr_by", "none"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  output = "kable"
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Only complete cases (in data and dif_var) are used, so at least one is needed.

dif_var

A vector (factor or character) of length nrow(data) with the groups, two or more.

cutoff

Optional. Default NULL, the partial gamma and its SE, with no test. Either of:

  • The full result of RMdifGammaCutoff(). This enables the bootstrap p-values (see p_value), and the caption reports the simulation settings.

  • Its $item_cutoffs data.frame alone, with columns Item, gamma_low and gamma_high. Items are flagged against the interval.

Either adds the columns Gamma_low, Gamma_high and a logical Flagged (TRUE when the partial gamma is outside the simulated interval, or with p-values when the item is flagged).

p_value

Logical or NULL. Whether to flag on two-sided bootstrap p-values (p_gamma, padj_gamma) from the simulations. The simulated interval is kept as a reference. TRUE needs the full RMdifGammaCutoff() result. NULL (default) uses the p-values whenever cutoff is that result, so a call without a cutoff gives no p-values. FALSE flags against the interval, a poor decision rule, since over k items a width w gives a family-wise error rate of 1 - w^k (Johansson, 2026).

correction

Character. Correction of the bootstrap p-values across items: "fwer" (default, Westfall-Young step-down), "fdr_bh", "fdr_by" or "none". Used only with p-values.

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). An item is flagged when its corrected p-value is below alpha. Default 0.05. Used only with p-values.

output

Character. "kable" (default) for a knitr::kable() table, or "dataframe".

Value

  • output = "kable": a knitr_kable table with the columns "Item", "Partial gamma" and "SE", plus "Gamma low", "Gamma high" and "Flagged" with a cutoff, and "p" and "p (adj)" with bootstrap p-values.

  • output = "dataframe": a data.frame with the columns Item, gamma and se, plus gamma_low, gamma_high and Flagged with a cutoff, and p_gamma and padj_gamma with bootstrap p-values.

Details

Statistic. The partial gamma (Bjorner et al., 1998) measures the association between the item response and an external grouping variable given the total score. Values near 0 indicate no DIF. Bjorner et al. (1998) also proposed classes of DIF size, which RMdifTree() uses. They are conventions, not values calibrated to the sample and items at hand, and this function does not use them. The iarm package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

No asymptotic test. iarm::partgam_DIF() also gives a p-value and a 95% interval from a normal approximation. In simulations without DIF (300 and 600 respondents), 15 dichotomous items had at least one item flagged after a Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment in 9% to 15% of datasets, because the test statistic has heavier tails than the normal. For 9 polytomous items the rate was 5% to 6.5%. Neither is returned. The SE matched the sampling SD of the partial gamma in these simulations. Test DIF with the result of RMdifGammaCutoff() as cutoff.

Bootstrap p-values. Each item's observed partial gamma is compared with its simulated values (cutoff$results, simulated without DIF). The statistic is the deviation from the mean of the observed and simulated values together, divided by their SD. The uncorrected p is two-sided, (1 + #\{|t*| >= |t|\}) / (B + 1) for B simulated datasets, so it can be no smaller than 1 / (B + 1). It is two-sided since DIF can favour either group, unlike RMlocdepGamma(), which tests one-sided for excess positive local dependence. correction = "fwer" uses the Westfall-Young step-down, which uses the dependence between the items (Westfall & Young, 1993, Ferreira, 2024). It controls the family-wise error rate at any number of iterations in RMdifGammaCutoff(), but below 400 decisions depend on the seed and a message says so. Unlike the asymptotic p-values, these are calibrated against simulations from the Rasch model. They depend on the model and the sample size, and are reported with the simulated interval, not instead of it. The observed partial gamma they test is computed by the same internal routine as the simulations, which reproduces iarm::partgam_DIF() exactly.

Real and artificial DIF. Partial gamma conditions on the total score, which includes every item. Real DIF in one item then induces artificial DIF in the other items, in the opposite direction, since at a given total score the item scores must add up to that score (Hagquist & Andrich, 2017). An item can therefore be flagged only because another item has DIF. The simulations in RMdifGammaCutoff() do not guard against this, since they have no DIF in any item. Resolve DIF items one at a time, starting with the largest, and repeat the analysis before deciding on the next (Hagquist & Andrich, 2017). RMdifAnchor() avoids the problem by linking the groups through anchor items.

Multiple comparisons

The uncorrected p-value controls the error rate of a single comparison. For one item (or item pair) chosen in advance it is the relevant value. Flagging whichever of k comparisons fall below alpha tests k hypotheses at once, and the chance of at least one false flag rises to about \(1 - (1 - \alpha)^k\), for example 34% for k = 8 at alpha = 0.05, even when every uncorrected p-value is calibrated. The corrected p-value controls this. correction = "fwer" bounds the probability of any false flag (strict, less power), and "fdr_bh" and "fdr_by" bound the expected share of false flags among those raised. Use the uncorrected p-value for a single comparison chosen in advance, and a corrected one when screening the whole table, which is the usual case.

References

Bjorner, J. B., Kreiner, S., Ware, J. E., Damsgaard, M. T., & Bech, P. (1998). Differential item functioning in the Danish translation of the SF-36. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 51(11), 1189–1202. doi:10.1016/S0895-4356(98)00111-5

Ferreira, J. A. (2024). Methods of testing a 'small' or 'moderate' number of hypotheses simultaneously. Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice, 19(1), 6. doi:10.1007/s42519-024-00412-4

Hagquist, C., & Andrich, D. (2017). Recent advances in analysis of differential item functioning in health research using the Rasch model. Health and Quality of Life Outcomes, 15, 181. doi:10.1186/s12955-017-0755-0

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

Westfall, P. H., & Young, S. S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing. Wiley.

See also

RMdifGammaCutoff() for the simulations, RMdifGammaPlot() for the plot, RMdifAnchor() for anchored tests, RMdifImpact() for the size of the impact.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)
  dif_group <- factor(sample(c("A", "B"), 200, replace = TRUE))

  # Default kable output
  RMdifGamma(sim_data, dif_group)

  # Return as data.frame
  RMdifGamma(sim_data, dif_group, output = "dataframe")

  # Simulation-based cutoffs (100 iterations to keep the example quick)
  if (requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cutoff_res <- RMdifGammaCutoff(sim_data, dif_var = dif_group,
                                   iterations = 100, parallel = FALSE,
                                   seed = 42)
    RMdifGamma(sim_data, dif_group, cutoff = cutoff_res)

    # The full cutoff object switches on bootstrap p-values with the
    # family-wise (Westfall-Young) correction. Use 1000 or more
    # iterations in real analyses.
    RMdifGamma(sim_data, dif_group, cutoff = cutoff_res,
               output = "dataframe")
  }
}
